# Nocturne Access: technical overview

**Status:** not yet public; work in progress. Development build 0.0.104 (October 2026).

**Authorship note:** this document was generated by an AI agent (Claude, Anthropic) that writes the mod's code, from the project's source code and engineering records. Testing and design decisions are by the project owner, a low-vision NVDA user.

## Scope

A screen-reader accessibility mod for Shin Megami Tensei III Nocturne HD Remaster (Steam, PC).

- Output: speech through NVDA (`nvdaControllerClient.dll`).
- Text sources: the game's own strings (text-component writes, the message engine, the game's data tables). No OCR. Numbers drawn as sprites are read from game data.
- License: GPL-3.0.

## Platform and toolchain

- Game engine: Unity 2019.4.10f1, IL2CPP backend.
- Loader: MelonLoader 0.6.1; the mod targets net6.0 and uses HarmonyX and Il2CppInterop.
- Hooks: Harmony postfixes, applied one by one, each logged; a failed hook does not stop the others.
- Research: read-only static analysis of `GameAssembly.dll` (method addresses from Cpp2IL metadata, disassembly of the field update, battle and menu code). The DRM-protected executable is never inspected.
- Offline data: asset bundles, field scripts (FlowScript procedures) and localization tables are read with project tools to classify events and find the game's own words.

## Architecture

- **Core:** one text hook on the TextMeshPro write path routes every write by its UI hierarchy path to the readers. Blank writes are discarded, and identical rewrites never count as activity.
- **Speech:** a background speech queue with interrupt and hold. A short ordering layer lets a screen's question be spoken before its options.
- **Readers:**
  - dialogue pages with speaker and choices;
  - menus whose cursor is a font material, plus menus whose cursor is a game object or a game cursor structure;
  - save and load lists, configuration, name entry;
  - status, item and skill lists, the fusion inheritance list;
  - shops, the Fountain of Life, the Terminal and Amala Link, Rag's Jewelry;
  - the Cathedral of Shadows' fusion tables (result icons in the game's own localized words) and the Demon Compendium.
- **Battle:** turn owner and press turns from the battle process data; actions, damage, healing, weakness, critical and miss results; HP and MP from unit data. Also skill costs and elements from the game's tables, affinities after Analyze, a battle log, summon lists with level, HP and MP, and results with spoils.

## Navigation

- **Data used:** player position and facing, area and field ids, every collision polygon of the loaded area, event volumes with their boxes, the door warp table (destinations, movement types), the NPC and item box tables, place-name pads, the game's collision switches and moving-object offsets, story flags.
- **Walking map:**
  - 30-unit cells holding up to 8 floor heights each;
  - walls by body overlap above each floor;
  - steps, risers and railings modelled on the game's own hit test (radius, test height);
  - moves reach every floor layer within a step;
  - trigger-only polygons excluded;
  - a separate rule set for the world map.

  A Dijkstra search and reachability flood run over it.
- **Points of interest:** doors (with the game's room names, kind and destination), exits, ladders, escalators, warps, people, demons, item boxes (opened or not), and events classified from their script procedures. They are listed in a fixed map order with filters.
- **Movement:** auto-walk and spoken directions to the selected point. Walking is driven only through the game's own pad-button input checks, at normal speed, so the game's collision, doors and events remain authoritative. Moves the game refuses are learned during a walk.
- **Links:** same-area door, ladder and warp pairs are chained in routes, and landmarks in other parts of an area are listed with their link count. Doors gone through are remembered per save file.
- **First person:** the game's locked first-person view is answered in memory only (the save is never written). An optional grid snap keeps the game's own controls; wall, opening and door cues speak only changes and never block input.
- **Puzzles:** for the Obelisk time puzzle, the next tile is derived from the field script's bridge variables and matched against published solutions.

## Diagnostics

- Per-session log archive.
- UI text dump.
- Navigation dump: collision, volumes, door table, walking map as text.
- Offline replicas of the walking map that rebuild reachability from any dump, used to check every rule change against all recorded areas before it ships.

## Development state

- Played through the story up to the Obelisk with the mod, including long sessions without sight.
- Each new area is tested in play. Failures are diagnosed from the session log and dumps, fixed and recorded.
- Not yet released; installation instructions and a public build will follow.
